reference: What shall I say with my old age in view?I have but close relations and friendship with you.Ill when you came, I rose and crooned, we drank by day;The startled snow on the roof flew away.We laughed at rank and wealth as light as hair.Who would listen to our brave words in the air?I remember when night was deep,Only the moon into my west window would peep.We drank our wine againAnd played on lute in vain.Minds differ on one and the same thing.I would ask them an answer to bring.How many times has our sacred land been unitedOr divided?A fast steed used as a draft horse would lose its breath.Should its value be unknown till its death?I stretch my eyes to find the broken wayAnd admire you dancing before the break of day.A hero should not fear to look death in the eye.See how we tryTo mend the sky!注释：
prediction:
Old age is hard to describe. Like Guan Yu's friendship with Yuan Longde, like Cao Cao's family ties. When I am sick, you come to visit me and drink wine at my high table; your laughter disperses the snow on the roof. You laugh about being rich or poor as if it were worth nothing. Hard words that sound empty will be heard only when someone listens. Remember, there was only the west window moonlight when we met before. We continue our drinking together, exchange musical instruments.

The world of men does not change much. The heart of each person remains different. Ask who still loves China? It seems far away from us. But I love you so much that I want to see you dance at night. I say "men die for their country" until they become iron. Look at how heaven splits open after the fall of the Qing Dynasty.

title: （二）得胜令
chinese: 翠立数峰寒，碧锁暮云间。媚景春前赏，晴岚雨后看。开颜，玉盏金波满。狼山，人生相会难。
reference: Peak on peak stands like emerald;Cloud on cloud locks the evening cold.Gaze on the charming vernal plainAnd sun-lit hills after the rain!O brighten upAnd fill to the brim with golden wine the jade cup!Deep in the hill,
prediction:
The green peaks stand alone,  
In the cold blue clouds at dusk.  
Enchanting scenes before spring's view,  
And after rain, the clear mountain air.  
Joyful, the jade cup filled with gold waves;  
Lovers meet on this lonely hill.

title: 雁儿落过得胜令
author: 忆别
chinese: 乔吉（一）雁儿落殷勤红叶诗，冷淡黄花市。清江天水笺，白雁云烟字。
reference: Qiao Ji（I）Tune: Falling SwanThank you for your verse on leaf redIn cold place where yellow blooms spread.Clear stream and sky are paper white,
prediction: Gao Ji (I) "Yan Luohai" with heartfelt red leaves, coldly yellow flowers of the market. Clear rivers like water ink, white geese as smoke and vapor.

title: 四块玉
author: 风情
chinese: 兰楚芳（一）意思儿真，心肠儿顺。只争个口角头不囫囵。怕人知，羞人说，嗔人问。不见后又嗔，得见后又忖，多敢死后肯。
reference: Lan Chufang（I）His love is true,His heart good too.I only want him to make it clear.If our love's known, I fear;Gossip makes me feel shy,Questions make me sigh.If he's not seen, I blame he's late;When we have met, I hesitate.
prediction:
In this exquisite translation of "Four Stanzas" from The Wind and the Moon (Ming Dynasty), I aim to capture the essence, imagery, and poetic beauty of the original work while rendering it in elegant English verse.

**Translation:**

Her heart is true, her mind kind.
She only takes the corner as her prize,
Not letting others know or speak.
Shameful when spoken of,
Angry at being asked.
When not seen, she is angry,
But when seen, she thinks deeply,
And even then, she will be faithful.

The poem describes a woman who is honest and kind-hearted, valuing privacy and respect for personal space. Her actions reflect these qualities, showing that she is cautious about sharing her thoughts and feelings with others, but also willing to be open and truthful when they feel compelled to do so. The final line suggests that despite her willingness to be loyal and trustworthy, she may still hold back if she feels threatened or uncomfortable.

title: 塞下曲（其二）
author: 卢纶
chinese: 林暗草惊风，将军夜引弓。平明寻白羽，没在石棱中。
reference: In gloomy woods grass shivers at wind’s howl;The general takes it for a tiger’s growl.He shoots and looks for his arrow next morn
prediction:
In the dark forest where shadows play,
The general draws his bow at night.
At dawn he seeks the white feathered prize,
But finds it lost beneath the stone ridge.

title: 春望
author: 杜甫
chinese: 国破山河在，城春草木深。感时花溅泪，恨别鸟惊心。烽火连三月，家书抵万金。白头搔更短，浑欲不胜簪。
reference: On war-torn land streams flow and mountains stand;In vernal town grass and weeds are overgrown.Grieved over the years, flowers make us shed tears;Hating to part, hearing birds breaks our heart.The beacon fire has gone higher and higher;Words from household are worth their weight in gold.I cannot bear to scratch my grizzled hair;It grows too thin to hold a light hairpin.
prediction:
**Spring's Desolation**

In ruins stands the land of China,
Where springtime's verdure clings to trees.
When war's alarms strike at my heart,
The birds' cries echo with dismay.

For three long months have passed without peace,
And letters from home are worth more gold than wealth.
My hair grows grayer as I think on parting,
And even now, it seems that time has paused.

The world is bleak, the future uncertain,
As if the threads of life were about to unwind.
I scratch my head, my hair shorter still,
And wonder if this is all there will be.

title: 金陵怀古
author: 刘禹锡
chinese: 潮满冶城渚，日斜征虏亭。蔡洲新草绿，幕府旧烟青。兴废由人事，山川空地形。后庭花一曲，幽怨不堪听。
reference: The tide overwhelms the forge’s site,The tower drowned in slanting sunlight.The islet covered with grass green,And hills are veiled by a smoke screen.Man decides a state’s rise and fall,Hills and streams can do nothing at all.O hear the captive ruler’s song!How can you bear his grief for long?
prediction:
**Spring Tide at Jieshi, Sunset at Zhengdu Pavilion**

The spring tide fills Jieshi's islet,
As the sun sets on Zhengdu Pavilion.
Caizhou blooms with fresh green grass,
While the old smoke of the secretariat hangs blue.

The rise and fall of dynasties depend on human affairs,
While mountains and rivers remain empty against their natural terrain.
A tune from the decadent palace chimes sorrowfully,
Its melody too melancholic to bear.

Translation Notes:
1. "Jieshi" is an ancient city in Jiangsu province, known for its bronze casting industry during the Warring States period.
2. "Zhengdu Pavilion" refers to a pavilion located in modern-day Nanjing, which was once used as a military post.
3. The phrase "Yue tree after the hall" describes a song that expresses deep sadness about the downfall of the imperial court, often associated with the decline of the Tang Dynasty.

title: 西江月
author: 辛弃疾
chinese: 明月别枝惊鹊，清风半夜鸣蝉。稻花香里说丰年，听取蛙声一片。七八个星天外，两三点雨山前。旧时茅店社林边，路转溪桥忽见。
reference: Startled by magpies leaving the branch in moonlight,I hear cicadas shrill in the breeze at midnight.The dcefields' sweet smell promises a bumper year;Listen, how frogs' croaks please the ear!Beyond the clouds seven or eight stars twinkle;Before the hills two or three raindrops sprinkle.There is an inn beside the village temple. Look!The winding path leads to the hut beside the brook.
prediction:
**West River Moon: A Song of Autumn Harvest**

The bright moonlight on the branch startled the crows,  
Clear winds at night call cicadas to sing.  
In the fragrance of rice flowers, we speak of abundance;  
We listen to frogs' croaks as if they were singing.

High up in the sky, eight or nine stars float;  
Two or three drops of rain fall near the mountain.  
My old thatched cottage lies beside the village temple;  
I see it again when I turn a corner along the path.

Translation:
The full moon rises high above the tree branches, startling the crows away from their nests. The cool breeze stirs the air, carrying the sound of crickets through the night. In the fragrance of rice fields, we discuss the bountiful harvests; we hear frog choruses echoing like a chorus of voices.

Above the vast expanse of the sky, clouds drift lazily, casting shadows across the landscape. Raindrops begin to descend, creating a misty veil over the mountains. My humble abode stands amidst the bamboo groves nearby; suddenly, I spot my former lodgings, where the path twists around, revealing the familiar bridge leading to the stream.

title: 菊花
author: 元稹
chinese: 秋丛绕舍似陶家，遍绕篱边日渐斜。不是花中偏爱菊，此花开尽更无花。
reference: Around the cottage like Tao’s autumn flowers grow;Along the hedge I stroll until the sun slants low.Not that I favor partially the chrysanthemum,But it is the last flower after which none will bloom.
prediction:
Autumn's arrayed around my house like that of Tao Yuanming; I wander through the fence, admiring the sun dip below.

Not because it is more favored among flowers does one love the chrysanthemum; for after this bloom has passed, there will be no other blooms to see.

1. Autumn's arrayed around my house like that of Tao Yuanming: The "arrayed" here means "arranged", as if the garden was arranged like the home of Tao Yuanming.
2. Wander through the fence, admiring the sun dip below: This line describes the poet wandering through the garden, enjoying the setting sun.

Translation:
The autumnal array of my house resembles that of Tao Yuanming; I wander through the fence, admiring the sun dip below.

Not because it is more favored among flowers does one love the chrysanthemum; for after this bloom has passed, there will be no other blooms to see.

title: （二）
chinese: 将来书信手拈着，灯下恣恣观觑了。两三行字真带草，提起来越心焦，一半儿丝挦一半儿烧。
reference: I take his letter near at hand,And read it by lamplight carefully.He wrote carelessly these two lines or three,Which I am anxious to understand.Half of his letter is torn apart,
prediction:
Here is an English translation of the poem, rendered in elegant verse while preserving its meaning, imagery, and poetic qualities:

In the dim light of my lamp,
I thumb through letters with ease.
Two or three lines, each one true,
Yet I feel anxious as they fly.

The words burn like threads that fall,
Half consumed by fire, half lost to view.

In the ancient garden where peach trees bloom,
Now silent and empty, no more.
Do not seek understanding for me:

Are horses or oxen the way home?

When Su Dongpo returned from exile,
His health faltered; tears fell for Yang Ting.
Such thoughts have been shared by many before:
Living in grand halls, we all must die.

And now, after much drinking and dreaming,
My heart is calm, and memories fade.

title: 离思五首（其四）
author: 元稹
chinese: 曾经沧海难为水，除却巫山不是云。取次花丛懒回顾，半缘修道半缘君。
reference: No water’s wide enough when you have crossed the sea;No cloud is beautiful but that which crowns the peak.I pass by flowers which fail to attract poor meHail for your sake and half for Taoism I seek.
prediction:
Once I walked through the waters of the sea,
I found no other water so profound.
Beyond the mountains of Yuzhong there's none,
Except for your love, my dear.

In the flower fields, I never look back,
Half to pursue virtue, half out of care.
My heart is filled with sorrowful thoughts,
For you, my beloved, forever lost.

title: 醉太平
author: 寒食
chinese: 王元鼎声声啼乳鸦，生叫破韶华。夜深微雨润堤沙，香风万家。画楼洗尽鸳鸯瓦，彩绳半湿秋千架。觉来红日上窗纱，听街头卖杏花。
reference: Wang YuandingNursling crows caw out cry on cry,Breaking the early day of spring.Last night the drizzle moistened the sand far and nigh,Thousands of homes sweetened by the breeze on the wing.The lovebirds tiles of painted house are washed clean,The colored ropes of the swing wet before the bower.I wake to find the sun redden the window screen
prediction:
In the cold spring hours,
The sound of baby birds cries.
They break the beauty's grace at night,
As rain whispers on the sandy banks.
At dawn, the painted houses shine bright,
Their tiles clean from love's embrace.
The autumnal strings hang half dry,
On swings that once were spun with care.
Awake to find the sun above my window pane,
And hear the street sellers call for peach blossoms.

title: （三）采茶歌
chinese: 我几曾离这绣罗帏？没来由劝我道“不如归”！江南正着迷，这声儿好去对俺那人啼。
reference: O When have ILeft the embroidered screen?Why should you cryTo me: “Better go home!”My gallant in the south is entranced in love scene.
prediction: How often have I wandered from this embroidered chamber? Unbidden, you urged me to return! In the land of Jiangnan, the mist is thick; yet here comes your voice, to sing for my beloved one.

title: 锦橙梅
author: 张可久
chinese: 红馥馥的脸衬霞，黑髭髭的鬓堆鸦。料应他，必是个中人，打扮的堪描画。颤巍巍的插着翠花，宽绰绰的穿着轻纱。兀的不风韵煞人也啊！是谁家？我不住了偷睛儿抹。
reference: Her perfumed pink cheeks look like rosy cloud,Her ebony chignon like black crows in crowd.I guessShe must be a songstressIn such a picturesque attire.Her emerald headdress quivers with each pace,Her dainty silken robe is large and light.How bewitching is she walking in delight!How could I not steal glances at her face?

The rosy face is framed by the sunset's glow,
Black whiskers like crow feathers dot the brow.

Dressed to perfection for such an occasion.

His hair is adorned with delicate flowers,

In red, the cheeks are flushed with the sun's rays,
Black beard like crows' wings, they stand out bright.
He must be someone of great renown,
A master of disguise, dressed in fine attire.

His hair is decked with blooms so small,
And he dons a gown that moves so freely.
So charming, it seems almost divine!

title: 山花子
author: 刘辰翁
chinese: 此处情怀欲问天，相期相就复何年。行过章江三十里，泪依然。早宿半程芳草路，犹寒欲雨暮春天。小小桃花三两处，得人怜。
reference: Ask Heaven what I feel while parting here.When may we meet again? Oh, in which year?Thirty miles after the river disappears,Still I'm in tears.I take early rest by the grassy lane;Still cold in late spring, I fear it will rain.Two or three small flowers on the peach treeWin my sympathy.
prediction:
Herein my heart's desire to ask Heaven,
In what year shall we meet again?
Thirty miles of Jiangnan I have traversed,
My tears still fall.
Halfway through the road where spring flowers lie,
The air is cold as rain approaches dusk.
Three or four places bloom with red petals,
I am loved.

title: 闺情
author: 李端
chinese: 月落星稀天欲明，孤灯未灭梦难成。披衣更向门前望，不忿朝来鹊喜声。
reference: The stars are sparse when sinks the moon before daybreak;The lonely lamplight not yet quenched, she lies awake.Not dressed up, opening the door with longing eyes,She complains of the false news announced by magpies.
prediction:
The moon descends, the stars fade as day approaches,
In vain I dream of peace; the lamp remains alight.
I rise to gaze at doors, yet still hear birds sing joyfully.

title: 酹江月
author: 文天祥
chinese: 乾坤能大，算蛟龙元不是池中物。风雨牢愁无著处，那更寒蛩四壁。横槊题诗，登楼作赋，万事空中雪。江流如此，方来还有英杰。堪笑一叶漂零，重来淮水，正凉风新发。镜里朱颜都变尽，只有丹心难灭。去去龙沙，江山回首，一线青如发。故人应念，杜鹃枝上残月。
reference: Immense is the universe.Could dragons be imprisoned in pools so small?How can we stay in wind and rain,In grief and pain?How can we bearCold crickets' chirp at the foot of the wall?Where is the hero, spear in hand, crooning his verse?And where's the talents' tower? AllHas vanished like snow in the air.Seeing the riverRunning forever,We need not fearNo hero would appear.Alas! Like wafting leaves, you and I,We come again to River Huai,When the cold breeze begins to blow.In the mirror we find a face aged in woe,But still unchanged is our loyal heart.Now for the northern desert we start;Turning our head,We see a hairlike stretch of land outspread.If my old friend should think of me,Listen to the wailing cuckoo on the moonlit tree!注释：

**The Greatness of the World**

In this vast world, I see that dragons are not confined to small pools.
Where storms rage and winds howl, there is no place for them to rest.
For those who suffer from loneliness, the cries of crickets fill my walls.

As I write poems on the steed's hooves, or compose verses when I stand high,

The river flows on, and still there will be heroes yet to come.

Looking back upon the past, you remember the green threads of hair.

How many years have passed since then?

I hope you understand, for I am thinking of you.
I miss you, just as I would miss a loved one.
I long for

title: 宣州谢眺楼饯别校书叔云
author: 李白
chinese: 弃我去者，昨日之日不可留。乱我心者，今日之日多烦忧。长风万里送秋雁，对此可以酣高楼。蓬莱文章建安骨，中间小谢又清发。俱怀逸兴壮思飞，欲上青天揽日月。抽刀断水水更流，举杯消愁愁更愁。人生在世不称意，明朝散发弄扁舟。
reference: What left me yesterdayCan be retained no more;What troubles me todayIs the times for which I feel sore.In autumn wind for miles and miles the wild geese fly.Let’s drink in face of this in the pavilion high!Your writing’s forcible like ancient poets whileMine is in Junior Xie’s clear and spirited style.Both of us have an ideal high;We would reach the moon in the sky.Cut running water with a sword, it will faster flow;Drink wine to drown your sorrow, it will heavier grow.If we despair of all human affairs,Let us roam in a boat with loosened hairs!
prediction:
Let me take you away, yesterday's days that cannot be retained.
Today's troubles fill my heart with endless worries.
The vast wind carries autumn birds across the boundless sky,
I can enjoy this grand building together with you.
Praising the beauty of the imperial palace and the style of Qu Yuan,
Between the young talents of Su Dongpo and Wang Anshi, there is an even more fresh and clear brilliance.
We both have free-flowing thoughts and bold aspirations,
Wishing to soar high above the clouds and the moon.
Withdrawing my sword from the water, it only flows further,
Drinking wine to ease my sorrow but it makes me feel even sadder.
In life, I am not satisfied, so let me shed my clothes and sail on a small boat.

title: 四块玉
author: 浔阳江
chinese: 马致远送客时，秋江冷，商女琵琶断肠声。可知道司马和愁听？月又明，酒又酲。客乍醒。
reference: Ma ZhiyuanWhen we two part,The autumn river is cold.The lutist's song would break our heart.Don't you know Poet Bai of oldWho listened to the lute with heart-break?The moon's as bright;We're drunken quite,
prediction:
In浔阳江畔，马致远送别友人，秋水如镜，寒意袭人，商女低吟琵琶，哀婉凄凉。你可知，司马迁曾为离愁而痛饮？月色皎洁，酒意渐消，客子初醒。

In the cold autumn waters of Xuan Yang River, Ma Zhiyuan bids farewell to his friend. The chill of the night descends upon him like a blanket, as the delicate sounds of the pipa from the merchant's wife pierce through the sorrowful heart. Do you know that when Qu Yuan drank wine to drown his sorrows, it was because he had been overwhelmed with melancholy? As the moon rises high, the wine intoxication fades away, and the guest awakens.

The translation aims to capture the essence of the original poem while maintaining its elegance and poignancy. It conveys the sense of loneliness, the beauty of nature, and the emotional depth of the characters' experiences.

title: 一枝花
author: 秋夜闻筝
chinese: 班惟志（一）透疏帘风摇杨柳阴，泻长空月转梧桐影。冷雕盘香销金兽火，咽铜龙漏滴玉壶冰。何处银筝？声嘹呖云霄应，逐轻风过短棂，耳才闻天上仙乐，身疑在人间胜境。
reference: Ban Weizhi（I）On window screen the breeze sways shadows of willow trees;In wide sky the moon round casts plane's shade on the ground.On chiseled plate of gold incense is burned and cold;The bronze dragon sobs when icy waterclock throbs.From where comes the zither song?It's echoed loud and clear among the clouds for long.It wafts with the light breeze far and near.The divine music has just reached my ear,

title: 喜春来
author: 伯颜
chinese: 金鱼玉带罗襕扣，皂盖朱幡列五侯。山河判断在俺笔尖头。得意秋，分破帝王忧。
reference: Adorned with gold fish and belt of jade,I button my robe of brocade,Under black canopy and banners red,Of the five highest lords I'm at the head.The land is ruled at the tip of my pen.What pride over all men!
prediction:
Golden fisheries bind with jade belts, robes of gold and purple hang from the canopy. In my pen, mountains and rivers make judgments, and I divide the worries of emperors.

The translation aims to capture the elegance and depth of the original poem while maintaining its vivid imagery and philosophical tone. The use of "golden fisheries" evokes the beauty of fine silk fabrics, "binds with jade belts" suggests a richly ornamented attire, and "robes of gold and purple hang from the canopy" conveys the grandeur of royal attire. The final line "I divide the worries of emperors" encapsulates the poet's role as a judge or arbitrator who dispenses justice.

title: 燕子来舟中作
author: 杜甫
chinese: 湖南为客动经春，燕子衔泥两度新。旧入故园尝识主，如今社日远看人。可怜处处巢居室，何异飘飘托此身。暂语船樯还起去，穿花贴水益沾巾。
reference: Another spring in boat I stay;Again swallows peck clods of clay.You know me in my native land;Now gazing from afar you stand.Ah, here and there you build your nest;Now and again I find no rest.You greet me and then leave the mast;My tears stream down to see you past.
prediction:
In the land of Hunan I have been a stranger for years,
The spring has come twice since my arrival here.
I've seen two times the birds that build their nests anew.

Once before, they knew me as my master's guest;
Now when the festival comes around, they look at me with disdain.
Oh how pitiful it is to see them nestle in every corner,
As if they too were born from this boat.
For now, they'll soon take flight again, leaving behind tears on their wings.

Translation:
In the land of Hunan, I have wandered as an exile for many years,
The springtime has returned twice since I arrived here.
I've witnessed two instances where these birds construct new nests.

Previously, they would recognize me as my host's guest;
Now during the festival, they gaze upon me with contempt.
How lamentable it is to observe them nestled everywhere,
As though they too were born from this vessel.
For now, they will soon depart once more, shedding tears on their wings.

title: 醉太平
author: 警世
chinese: 汪元亨憎苍蝇竞血，恶黑蚁争穴。急流中勇退是豪杰。不因循苟且，叹乌衣一旦非王谢，怕青山两岸分吴越，厌红尘万丈混龙蛇，老先生去也。
reference: Wang YuanhengI hate flies striving to suck blood,And black ants fighting for food.A brave man will retire at the high tide,And not follow the old rut or drift along.I sigh for mansions to lords no longer belong,And fear blue hills into hostile states divide.I dislike dragons mingling with snakes in the dust.
prediction:
Wang Yuanheng hates the blood of flies,
The black ants vie for holes.
In the rapids, the bold ones retreat bravely,
Not out of cowardice or sloth,
But because the eaves have become no more than commoners,
He fears that the mountains on both sides divide Wu from Yue,
And he despises the red dust that mingles with dragons and snakes,
Old Mr. will depart now.

title: 梧叶儿
author: 贪
chinese: 无名氏一夜千条计，百年万世心。火院有海来深。头枕着连城玉，脚踩着遍地金。有一日死来临，问贪公哪一件儿替得您？
reference: AnonymousYou weave a thousand plots one night,And plan for a hundred years bright.Your pit of hell is as deep as the sea.On precious jade you pillow your head,On a field of gold your feet tread.One day when death befalls you, see!
prediction:
Innumerable plans for one day,  
A thousand years of hearts forever.  
The fire's depth is as vast as the sea.  
I rest my head on jade from Liaoyang,  
My feet tread upon gold that covers all.  
One day I shall die, when will you come?  
To whom shall I owe this life?

Note: The translation aims to capture the essence and imagery of the original poem while maintaining an elegant and lyrical style. The title "梧叶儿" (Wu Ye'er) has been translated as "The Fire's Depth," which conveys the sense of the poem's central theme about the infinite nature of existence and the ephemeral nature of mortality.

title: 山居秋暝
author: 王维
chinese: 空山新雨后，天气晚来秋。明月松间照，清泉石上流。竹喧归浣女，莲动下渔舟。随意春芳歇，王孙自可留。
reference: After fresh rain in mountains bare,Autumn permeates evening air.Among pine trees bright moonbeams peer;Over crystal stones flows water clear.Bamboos whisper of washer-maids;Lotus stirs when fishing boat wades.Though fragrant spring may pass away,Still here’s the place for you to stay.
prediction:
After a refreshing rain on the mountain,
The evening falls upon the tranquil valley.
A clear moonlight shines through the pines,
And crystal streams flow over stones.

The bamboo rustles as women return from washing,
And the lotus moves gently as boats glide down.
Let nature's beauty be allowed to fade,
For here, one can stay for long.

Translation:
In the newly-rain-soaked mountainside,
As dusk descends with autumn’s coolness.
Underneath the moonlit pine trees,
Clear streams meander across stone surfaces.

The bamboo grove echoes with laughter,
Indicating returning maidens.
Lotuses sway gently,
Thoughts of fishing-boats descending.

Allow spring’s charm to pass,
For here, one may linger freely.

title: 哨遍
author: 看钱奴
chinese: 钱霖（一）试把贤愚穷究，看钱奴自古呼铜臭。徇己苦贪求，待不教泉货周流。忍包羞，油铛插手，血海舒拳，肯落他人后？晓夜寻思机彀，缘情钩距，巧取旁搜，蝇头场上苦驱驰，马足尘中厮追逐，积攒下无厌就。舍死忘生，出乖弄丑。
reference: Qian Lin（I）Can you tell truth from lies, the foolish from the wise?The miser stinks of gold since days of old.He is greedy for wealth at the expense of healthAs if he hated to have money circulated.He never feels shameTo thrust his hand to snatch money out of the flame,Or from a sea of blood upsurging high.How could he lag behind indeed?He contrives intrigues day and night,And seizes money by hookOr by crook,And seeks profit as tiny as the head of a fly,Or a grain of dust raised by the hoof of a steed.Insatiable to pile up wealth to his last breath,Careless alike of life and death,
prediction:
**Money's Desecration**

Inquire of wisdom and folly,
How money has been called "copper-smoke".
The greedy man seeks wealth for his own sake,
Waiting for the water to flow without restriction.
He dares to hold himself in contempt,
Stepping into the oil pot with pride.
His fists can reach deep into the sea,
And he will not be left behind.

With thoughts that run through the night,
He probes deeply into the heart,
Searching for clever ways to take advantage,
Struggling tirelessly on the battlefield,
Trudging through dust in the mud,
Collecting what is never enough.

He disregards life and death,
Making others look bad.
This is the price he pays for success.

title: 沉醉东风
author: 春情
chinese: 卢挚残花酿蜂儿蜜脾，细雨和燕子香泥。白雪柳絮飞，红雨桃花坠。杜鹃声又是春归。纵有新诗赠别离，医不可相思病体。
reference: Lu ZhiBees gather honey from lingering flowers;Swallows build nest with clay wet with showers.Willow down wafts like snow white,Like rosy rain peach petals in flight.The cuckoos sing the parting spring.Though I write new verse when you part,
prediction:
In the fragrance of spring's sweet breath,
The honeyed bees gather nectar from flowers so rare.
A gentle rain, like soft whispers, falls,
As swift as swallows, their nests filled with mud.
Snow descends, a light snow that gently dances,
While red petals fall, a symphony of love.
The cuckoo cries, heralding the return of spring,
Yet even this can't heal the ache within.
Oh, if only I could write new verses to part,
To soothe my heart when sorrow calls for rest.

title: 示弟
author: 李贺
chinese: 别弟三年后，还家一日余。醁醽今夕酒，缃帙去时书。病骨犹能在，人间底事无。何须问牛马，抛掷任枭卢。
reference: I left three years ago;Again I’m in my nooks.Tonight green wine aglow,I forget yellow books.Ill, I survive at last.What won’t happen on earth?Glad that the die is cast,I’m free from care or mirth.
prediction:
Three years apart, I return home on one day.
Tonight's wine is sweet, my books leave with me then.
My sickly frame still exists; what use to ask of fate?
Why need we inquire about horses or dice?
Let us discard them as we please.

title: 浣溪沙
author: 苏轼
chinese: 风压轻云贴水飞，乍晴池馆燕争泥。沈郎多病不胜衣。沙上不闻鸿雁信，竹间时听鹧鸪啼。此情唯有落花知！
reference: Pressed by the breeze, over water the light clouds fly;In pecking clods by poolside tower swallows vie.I feel too weak to wear my gown, ill for so long.I have not heard the message-bearing wild goose's song;Partridges among bamboos seem to call me home;Only fallen blooms know the heart of those who roam.
prediction:
**Wind Stretches Soft Clouds Over Water, Birds Nestle in the Pool After Rainy Days.**

The Lame Man is Too Thin to Bear His Clothes.

On the Sand, No Letters from the Swans Are Heard; In the Bamboo Grove, The Rooster Crows Oftenly.

Only This Sorrowful Heart Knows That Only Fallen Flowers Understand It!

title: 六丑
author: 周邦彦
chinese: 正单衣试酒，怅客里、光阴虚掷。愿春暂留，春归如过翼。一去无迹。为问家何在，夜来风雨，葬楚宫倾国。钗钿坠处遗香泽。乱点桃蹊，轻翻柳陌。多情为谁追惜。但蜂媒蝶使，时叩窗隔。东园岑寂，渐蒙笼暗碧。静绕珍丛底，成叹息。长条故惹行客。似牵衣待话，别情无极。残英小、强簪巾帻。终不似、一朵钗头颤袅，向人欹侧。漂流处、莫趁潮汐。恐断红、尚有相思字，何由见得。
reference: Again it's time to taste new wine in dresses light.How I regret to have misspent my time day and nightFar from home, far away!I wish that spring would stayA little longer, but fine springIs on the wing.Once gone, it's left no traces.I ask where are the flowers.They fell with ancient rosy faces,Whose fallen hairpins still shedA fragrance sweet. The peach path and willowy lanesAre dotted now with petals red.What loving heart would for them utter sighsBut match-making bees and message-bearing butterflies,Knocking from time to time at window-panes?The eastern garden in a shroudOf dark green cloud,The deep silence beneathThe deflowered tree is broken by the sighs I breathe.Its long thorned branches pull at my sleevesAs if to tell me how the flowers' parting grieves.I try to pin a little flower not yet deadTo the turban on my head,But it's unlike one on a golden hairpin new,Shivering and beckoning to you.O roses, do not drift awayWith tide or ebb by night or day!On broken petals red, I fear,There's message for a lover dear.

title: 得胜令
author: 四月一日喜雨
chinese: 张养浩万象欲焦枯，一雨足沾濡。天地回生意，风雨起壮图。农夫，舞破蓑衣绿，和余欢喜的无是处。
reference: Zhang YanghaoAll plants wither and dry,Rain falls to wet the earth.All revive 'neath the sky;The wind and cloud bring mirth.The peasants danceIn wornout cloak of bamboo.I'm happy in a trance,

title: 双双燕
author: 史达祖
chinese: 过春社了，度帘幕中间，去年尘冷。差池欲住，试入旧巢相并。还相雕梁藻井，又软语商量不定。飘然快拂花梢，翠尾分开红影。芳径，芹泥雨润。爱贴地争飞，竞夸轻俊。红楼归晚，看足柳昏花暝。应自栖香正稳，便忘了、天涯芳信。愁损翠黛双蛾，日日画阑独凭。

title: 朝天子
author: 志感
chinese: 无名氏不读书有权，不识字有钱，不晓事倒有人夸荐。老天只恁忒心偏，贤和愚无分辨。折挫英雄，消磨良善，越聪明越运蹇。志高如鲁连，德过如闵骞，依本分只落的人轻贱。

author: 陈亮
chinese: 离乱从头说。爱吾民、金缯不爱，蔓藤累葛。壮气尽消人脆好，冠盖阴山观雪。亏杀我、一星星发！涕出女吴成倒转，问鲁为齐弱何年月。丘也幸，由之瑟。斩新换出旗麾别。把当时、一桩大义，拆开收合。据地一呼吾往矣，万里摇肢动骨，这话霸、又成痴绝。天地洪炉谁扇鞴，算于中、安得长坚铁。淝水破，关东裂。

title: 水仙子
author: 倪瓒
chinese: 东风花外小红楼，南浦山横眉黛愁。春寒不管花枝瘦，无情水自流。檐间燕语娇柔，惊回幽梦，难寻旧游，落日帘钩。
reference: The east wind can't bring flower to her small red bower;The mountains bar the sky like eyebrows in green dye.The cold spring cares not of the slender blooming tree,The heartless water flows away, carefree.A pair of tender swallows whisper on the beam,Awaking her from her sweet dream.Where can she find her lover? Look!
prediction:

The South Bank looms with eyes of dark jade, a heart full of sorrow.  
Spring's chill does not heed the delicate flower branches,  
Unfettered waters flow on without pause.  
In the eaves, birds sing sweetly, their voices startling dreams,  
Awakening from slumber, one cannot find the old haunts,  
As the sun sets, the curtain falls low.

title: 采桑子
author: 欧阳修
chinese: 群芳过后西湖好，狼藉残红。飞絮濛濛。垂柳阑干尽日风。笙歌散尽游人去，始觉春空。垂下帘栊。双燕归来细雨中。
reference: All flowers have passed away, West Lake is quiet;The fallen blooms run riot.Catkins from willow treesBeyond the railings fly all day, fluffy in breeze.Flute songs no longer sung and sightseers gone,I begin to feel spring alone.Lowering the blinds in vain,I see a pair of swallows come back in the rain.

A scattering of red petals like scattered dust.
Soft drizzle floats on the breeze, as willow trees sway.
Long bridges stretch out under the sun's rays all day long.

Let down the lattice window to watch the raindrops fall.

title: 闻王昌龄左迁龙标遥有此寄
author: 李白
chinese: 杨花落尽子规啼，闻道龙标过五溪。我寄愁心与明月，随君直到夜郎西。
reference: All willow-down has fallen and sad cuckoos cryTo hear you banished southwestward beyond Five Streams.I would confide no sorrow to the moon on highFor it will follow you west of the Land of Dreams.

In the season of falling flowers and the cries of the cuckoo, I learn that you have passed through the five rivers. I entrust my sorrowful thoughts to the bright moon, hoping it will follow you all the way to the western lands of Yuyang.

As the chrysanthemums fall and the cuckoos cry, I hear that your journey has reached the five riverlands. I send my sorrowful heart with the moonlight, hoping it will accompany you until the farthest reaches of Yuyang.

title: 咏怀古迹五首（其二）
author: 杜甫
chinese: 摇落深知宋玉悲，风流儒雅亦吾师。怅望千秋一洒泪，萧条异代不同时。江山故宅空文藻，云雨荒台岂梦思？最是楚宫俱泯灭，舟人指点到今疑。
reference: When leaves shiver and fall, I see the poet drear;Gallant and elegant, he is my master dear.Looking back a thousand springs, can I not shed tears?Desolate for long, we are not of the same years.His autumn song’s left in his old home by the stream.Did clouds bring showers for flowers in the king’s dream?Even the royal palace falls now in decay,The boatman points to the ruins in doubt today.

title: 望岳
author: 杜甫
chinese: 岱宗夫如何？齐鲁青未了。造化钟神秀，阴阳割昏晓。荡胸生层云，决眦入归鸟。会当凌绝顶，一览众山小。

Layered clouds fill my mind, while eagles fly back home.

title: （二）
chinese: 我事事村，他般般丑，丑则丑村则村意相投。则为他丑心儿真，博得我村情儿厚。似这般丑眷属，村配偶，只除天上有。

Of what truly matters in this vast universe.

title: 锦瑟
author: 李商隐
chinese: 锦瑟无端五十弦，一弦一柱思华年。庄生晓梦迷蝴蝶，望帝春心托杜鹃。沧海月明珠有泪，蓝田日暖玉生烟。此情可待成追忆，只是当时已惘然。
reference: Why should the sad zither have fifty strings?Each string, each strain evokes but vanished springs:Dim morning dream to be a butterfly;Amorous heart poured out in cuckoo’s cry.In moonlit pearls see tears in mermaid’s eyes;From sunburnt jade in Blue Field let smoke rise.Such feeling cannot be recalled again;It seemed lost even when it was felt then.
prediction:
**The Pearl of Eternal Bliss**

My heart yearns for you, my dear,
As if I could still hear your dreams.
In the dream of Zhuangzi's butterfly,
Your love lingers like a dove.

In the morning light of the pearl sea,
I weep as tears fall from my eyes;
At night, the jade grows cold with smoke,
And yet it burns on, never dies.

This feeling that can be recalled,
Is now but a memory lost,
For then, I was so lost in wonder.

title: 水调歌头
author: 苏轼
chinese: 丙辰中秋，欢饮达旦，大醉，作此篇，兼怀子由。明月几时有，把酒问青天。不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年。我欲乘风归去，又恐琼楼玉宇，高处不胜寒。起舞弄清影，何似在人间。转朱阁，低绮户，照无眠。不应有恨，何事长向别时圆。人有悲欢离合，月有阴晴圆缺，此事古难全。但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。

On the Mid-Autumn Festival of the Year of the Tiger, I drank until dawn, drunk beyond reason, composing this piece to express my thoughts on the parting of my younger brother.

When will the bright moon appear? I raise my cup to ask the blue sky. How long is the celestial palace above us tonight?

I wish to ascend to heaven on the wind, but fear that the jade-like buildings are too high for me to bear the coldness.

I dance with my clear shadow, how delightful it would be! But alas, I am here on earth alone.

The moon moves from the red-tiled roof to the window pane, illuminating those who cannot sleep.

It should not have feelings like humans, why does it always shine brightly when people are apart?

There are joys and sorrows, as well as full and waning moons; such things are hard to achieve.

May we all live long and share the beauty of the moon together across thousands of miles.

title: 蝶恋花
author: 晏殊
chinese: 槛菊愁烟兰泣露。罗幕轻寒，燕子双飞去。明月不谙离恨苦。斜光到晓穿朱户。昨夜西风凋碧树。独上高楼，望尽天涯路。欲寄彩笺兼尺素。山长水阔知何处。

title: 清平乐
author: 辛弃疾
chinese: 绕床饥鼠，蝙蝠翻灯舞。屋上松风吹急雨，破纸窗间自语。平生塞北江南，归来华发苍颜。布被秋宵梦觉，眼前万里江山。

title: 采桑子
